name: SAML Request Tracer successor
demand: There is clear use, but no verified willingness to pay. The current SimpleSAMLphp SAML-tracer listing shows 400,000 Chrome users and an update on 2026-08-20 (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/saml-tracer/mpdajninpobndbfcldcmbpnnbhibjmch); its Firefox listing shows 21,442 users and an update on 2026-07-30 (https://addons.mozilla.org/en-US/firefox/addon/saml-tracer/). The removed SAML Request Tracer's 27,000+ users are an AppBox operator's May 2026 report, not independently verified store data (https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg). Vendor support and developer documentation from GitLab and Okta recommend SAML-tracing tools for troubleshooting, which supports a recurring use case but does not quantify its market (https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/saml_sso/troubleshooting/; https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/saml-tracer/main/). No reliable search-volume or regulated-population figure verified.
prices: The current Awesome SAML Tracer listing says it is free (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/awesome-saml-tracer/pilkjgooejhajccieiebbihilnclbpej); the incumbent is described as free and is BSD-licensed (https://www.myworkdrive.com/kb/articles/troubleshooting-saml-saml-tracer; https://github.com/simplesamlphp/SAML-tracer); SAML Chrome Panel is open source (https://github.com/milton-lai/saml-chrome-panel). No verified paid team plan or sales found. A separate site, samltracer.com, advertises $2.90/month and $9.90 lifetime, but its install link resolves to an empty-title Chrome Store page, so treat both the price and product availability as unverified (https://samltracer.com/; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/empty-title/gjhodfmodljmmndflcilhkbikpcclkjn).

revenue_proof.claim: UNVERIFIED, zero revenue weight: AppBox's 2026-05-27 post says a significant share of affected extensions' users were paying subscribers and lists SAML Request Tracer at 27,000+ users. It gives no revenue, paying-user count, or extension-specific payment evidence (https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg).

copy_speed: One date-verified direct launch falls within the rolling six months before 2026-10-23: Awesome SAML Tracer, created 2026-05-19. It offers SAML decoding, formatted attributes, export/sharing, and is free; Chrome's listing shows 3,000 users, while Chrome-Stats reported 4,000 on 2026-10-23, so the counts differ (https://chrome-stats.com/d/pilkjgooejhajccieiebbihilnclbpej; https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/awesome-saml-tracer/pilkjgooejhajccieiebbihilnclbpej). Entra Auth Tracer is a relevant SAML-capable adjacent tool: its Chrome-Stats creation date is 2026-04-07, and its author says it later reached the Chrome Store, but the exact public launch date is unverified (https://chrome-stats.com/d/phnebijghhehloikpgohcblcljkaokbh; https://www.linkedin.com/posts/darrenjrobinson_entra-auth-tracer-a-browser-extension-for-activity-7443070071381430272-RoWE). Its first-party article is dated 2026-03-27 (https://blog.darrenjrobinson.com/author/darrenjrobinson/). On strictly dated launches after 2026-04-23, the two-launch threshold is not evidenced; counting calendar-month creation dates from April 1 would include Entra Auth Tracer and Awesome SAML Tracer. The June 1 SAMLScope page is a review claiming availability, not verified launch evidence (https://toolsforchrome.com/samlscope-saml-tracer-chrome-extension-review).
platform_risk: Chrome DevRel said on 2026-07-07 that third-party monetization is allowed, but paywall libraries must be disclosed and data collection must follow store policies; on 2026-07-10 the same representative said the removal actions were considered correct. So subscriptions are not stated to be categorically banned, but enforcement risk and limited case-specific explanation are real (https://groups.google.com/a/chromium.org/g/chromium-extensions/c/m9V8BJOgTEg). The tool handles authentication data: the current listing declares that SAML-tracer handles personally identifiable and authentication information, while Chrome policy requires narrow permissions, data disclosures, and secure handling (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/saml-tracer/mpdajninpobndbfcldcmbpnnbhibjmch; https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/policies/). Local-only processing, minimal permissions, redaction, and clear disclosures should be core requirements.
defensible_asset: No unique UK data asset or strong moat identified. The incumbent is BSD-2 licensed, and new tools already reuse its export format or describe themselves as forks, making basic capture and decoding readily reproducible (https://github.com/simplesamlphp/SAML-tracer; https://github.com/jsegers1974/awesome-saml-tracer; https://github.com/darrenjrobinson/EntraAuthTracer). A plausible differentiator is a maintained local rules engine that explains common IdP/SP configuration failures, backed by versioned, sanitized test fixtures and safe team handoffs; that asset and its demand are unvalidated.
build_effort: Moderate for a polished local-only extension; higher for paid team sync, accounts, and billing. The scope includes cross-browser capture, SAML parsing, useful diagnostics, export/redaction, permissions, and store releases. Public BSD-licensed code and existing implementations reduce the starting work, but sensitive authentication handling still needs human security review (https://github.com/simplesamlphp/SAML-tracer; https://github.com/jsegers1974/awesome-saml-tracer; https://developer.chrome.com/docs/webstore/program-policies/mv3-requirements). Exact build hours are unverified. No product is running, so 0% automation is currently demonstrated; the prospective automation share is unverified.
channel: Use inbound browser-store discovery, GitHub, and search-focused troubleshooting guides; GitLab and Okta already publish SAML-tracer instructions that show how this audience finds tools (https://docs.gitlab.com/user/group/saml_sso/troubleshooting/; https://developer.okta.com/docs/guides/saml-tracer/main/). Public technical posts and opt-in communities do not require Ricardo's face or personal brand. Do not use cold email, SMS, WhatsApp, or private social DMs to individuals or sole traders: ICO guidance includes private social DMs as electronic mail and generally requires consent for marketing to individual subscribers, including sole traders (https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guidance-on-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/key-concepts-for-direct-marketing-using-electronic-mail/; https://ico.org.uk/for-organisations/direct-marketing-and-privacy-and-electronic-communications/guide-to-pecr/electronic-and-telephone-marketing/electronic-mail-marketing/).
owner_hours_per_week: Unverified; the business has no operating baseline. The <=5 h/week target is not evidenced and should be measured in a pilot. It is more plausible for a local-only free core with automated build/release and support triage than for a hosted team product.
desk_test: One-day, no-code test: make a truthful landing page with a short mockup of local redaction and a team handoff, plus an optional form asking whether visitors would trial paid team features and what they would pay. Share only through public technical communities that permit promotion and relevant GitHub/docs surfaces; use explicit opt-in before any follow-up. Continue only if independent IAM practitioners volunteer concrete paid-team use cases; otherwise kill. Do not claim a working product or collect trace data.
red_flags: The successor premise is weaker than it first appeared: the canonical SimpleSAMLphp SAML-tracer remains listed at 400,000 Chrome users and was updated in August 2026, so the category is not vacant (https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/saml-tracer/mpdajninpobndbfcldcmbpnnbhibjmch). The reported 27,000-user removal is self-reported, current alternatives are free, and there is no verified revenue or buyer evidence. A generic clone is easy to copy; monetization and store enforcement add platform risk. The <=5 h/week and >=50% automation constraints remain unproven. Treat this as conditional on a paid-team demand test and a genuine diagnostic/workflow differentiator.
